newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper meet ends with no accord - radio.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper meet ends with no accord - radio.

text.p: A meeting between management and striking miners at the Neves Corvo copper mine ended on Thursday without any accord on ending a four-day-old strike, local radio TSF said in a report from the mine 250 km southeast of Lisbon.
Officials could not immediately be contacted for comment.
A mine official subsequently confirmed to Reuters that the meeting had ended in deadlock.
Alcides Pereira, chairman of Somincor, the state-owned company that runs the mine, was giving a news conference at the site, the official added.
Union officials, who said earlier they would step up their protest with demonstrations in Lisbon on Thursday if no accord was reached, were holding meetings with striking workers.
The strike at the 107,000 tonne per year mine began on Monday after the company introduced Sunday shifts in a bid to boost efficiency.
